channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kazakhstan Lost 40,000 Scientists Since USSR Collapse, Minister Says
item.description: Kazakhstan lost a significant portion of its scientists after the collapse of the USSR, with many transitioning to roles in government and banking, according to Minister of Science and Higher Education Sayasat Nurbek. In 1990, the country had 52,000 scientific and technical workers; by 2000, only 12,000 remained. The minister cited this decline as a primary reason for the current weakness of science in Kazakhstan.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Security Services Uncover Theft of Power Line Wires at Osh Energy Enterprise
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's State Committee for National Security (GKNB) has uncovered systematic theft and illegal sale of aluminum wires from the Osh enterprise of electric networks (Osh-PESS). The head of the central warehouse allegedly sold materials intended for repairing power transmission lines. This shortage poses risks for timely repairs ahead of the autumn-winter period.

item.title: Mobile Phones Dominate Kyrgyzstan's Exports to UAE, Driven by Re-exports
item.description: In 2025, electronics, primarily mobile phones, accounted for 80-87% of Kyrgyzstan's exports to the UAE, largely consisting of re-exports, according to the Eurasian Development Bank. Kyrgyzstan's trade with Gulf countries has grown ninefold since 2020. While electronics lead, Kyrgyzstan also increases food and industrial goods exports, while importing cars and cosmetics from the Gulf.

item.title: Former Kyrgyz Foreign Minister Aidarbekov Confirms Dropping Criminal Case, Explains Mandate Resignation
item.description: Former Kyrgyz Foreign Minister and ex-MP Chingiz Aidarbekov announced the complete closure of a criminal case against him, citing the absence of a crime event. He also explained his decision to resign his parliamentary mandate and addressed potential presidential election participation. Aidarbekov presented documents confirming the case's termination and his legal victories in previous proceedings.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Education Minister Comments on Student's Death in Almaty
item.description: Minister of Science and Higher Education Sayasat Nurbek addressed the death of a student in Almaty. He stated that Al-Farabi Kazakh National University has not yet issued an official statement due to an ongoing investigation. The Almaty police department has cautioned university representatives to be careful with any statements. The ministry has contacted the student's guardians.

item.title: Bishkek Heating Season Begins Amidst Expected Cold Snap, CHP Operates Normally
item.description: Bishkek's combined heat and power plant (CHP) is operating normally, providing heat and electricity to the capital as temperatures are forecast to drop significantly. Emergency crews are on standby for potential issues. The heating season commenced on October 28th, considering temperature drops and grid load.

item.title: UN Warns Rising Fertilizer Prices Could Impact Afghanistan's Agricultural Yields
item.description: The UN's Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) warns that rising fertilizer prices and limited access to agricultural inputs could reduce the benefits of the El Niño phenomenon for Afghanistan's crops. Over 1.7 million farming families require emergency agricultural aid. FAO has launched a project to strengthen the sector against climate change.

item.title: Atyrau Deputy Akim Resigns Amid Corruption Allegations
item.description: The deputy akim of Atyrau has resigned from his post. His resignation follows earlier suspicions and investigations into alleged corruption. The specific details of the corruption allegations have not been fully disclosed.

item.title: ADB Approves $60 Million Loan to Boost Uzbekistan's Livestock Sector
item.description: The Asian Development Bank (ADB) has approved a $60 million concessional loan to enhance productivity and sustainability in Uzbekistan's livestock sector. The project will support nearly 29,000 smallholder farms across several regions, improving fodder access and veterinary services.

item.title: Afghan United Front Claims Execution of Two Individuals in Ghor Province
item.description: The Afghan United Front, led by Sami Sadat, announced the execution of two individuals in Ghor province, accusing them of spying for the Taliban. The group released videos showing the alleged executions. This follows previous claims by the front of executing six individuals for similar alleged offenses.

item.title: Toktogul HPP Modernization Project Recognized Internationally
item.description: The large-scale modernization project of the Toktogul Hydroelectric Power Plant (HPP) has been shortlisted for the POWER Top Plant award by the international industry publication POWER Magazine. The project increased the plant's capacity from 1,200 MW to 1,440 MW without a full shutdown, a method experts deem unique.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan President Sadyr Japarov Collects Maximum Signatures for Election Bid
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's incumbent President Sadyr Japarov has collected the maximum allowable number of voter signatures for his presidential election candidacy in less than 24 hours. He submitted his self-nomination application on November 10. The electronic system shows 60,000 signatures, the legal maximum, were gathered.

item.title: Schoolchildren's personal data exposed in Kazakhstan's Kostanay region
item.description: The prosecutor's office in Kazakhstan's Kostanay region has identified violations of personal data protection for children. Two schools transferred student information to service organizations without parental consent. Personal data of minors was also found publicly accessible on a school's website. Officials responsible have been fined.

item.title: EBRD plans €1 billion infrastructure program for Kyrgyzstan
item.description: The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) is preparing an infrastructure investment program for Kyrgyzstan estimated at €1 billion. Priorities include green energy, infrastructure, and support for small and medium-sized businesses. The bank aims to expand its geographical reach within the country.

item.title: Kazakhstan Railways to deploy Stadler trains on most routes by 2030
item.description: Kazakhstan Temir Zholy (KTZ) plans to operate Stadler passenger trains on nearly all major routes by 2030. The company expects to receive a total of 660 new wagons by the end of the decade, with deliveries ongoing. New trains are being introduced on routes from Astana to Almaty and Semey.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's First Deputy Prime Minister Attends COP31 Leaders Summit in Antalya
item.description: Adylbek Kasymaliyev, First Deputy Chairman of the Cabinet of Ministers of Kyrgyzstan, attended the opening ceremony of the Leaders Summit within COP31 in Antalya, Turkey. He met with Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan and UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres. Other Kyrgyz officials present included the special representative for the president's agenda, the minister of natural resources, and the ambassador to Turkey.

item.title: Amur Ayba Meder Submits Application to Run for President of Kyrgyzstan
item.description: Amur Ayba Meder has submitted an application to the Central Election Commission of Kyrgyzstan to be nominated as a presidential candidate. Limited information is available about the contender in open sources, though business registries indicate a person with the same name heads companies involved in oil product processing and tourism. Confirmation that this individual is the presidential hopeful is pending.

item.title: Kazakhtelecom to Establish Credit Line with Citibank for Trade Financing
item.description: Kazakhtelecom's board of directors has approved an agreement with Citibank Europe PLC to establish a non-binding credit line for trade financing. The line will be at least 10% of the company's equity, approximately 73.2 billion tenge as of July 1, 2026.

item.title: Nearly 3.7 Kilograms of Drugs Seized in Operations Across Four Uzbek Regions
item.description: Security forces in Uzbekistan have seized approximately 3.67 kilograms of various drugs, including hashish, synthetic narcotics, and opium, during operations in Syrdarya, Navoi, Samarkand, and Karakalpakstan. Several individuals suspected of drug trafficking and distribution were detained.

item.title: Almaty Section of Alatau Avenue to Close for Metro Construction
item.description: A section of Alatau Avenue in Almaty will be partially closed to traffic starting November 13th for the construction of a new metro station. The closure affects the stretch between Abay Avenue and Ulugbek Street. Drivers can use a detour. The third phase of the first metro line includes 5.3 km of tunnels and three new stations.

item.title: Osh Airport Undergoing Major Renovation and Expansion
item.description: Osh International Airport in Kyrgyzstan is undergoing significant construction and renovation. A new 25,000 square meter terminal for international flights is being built, while the current terminal will be renovated for domestic flights. The runway will be extended by 400 meters, and aircraft parking capacity will increase.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's 'Tunuk' App Now Allows Users to Track Personal Data Requests
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's 'Tunuk' government services app and portal have launched a new feature enabling citizens to check which state bodies and organizations have requested their personal data, and when and why. The 'Request History' section displays metadata of data processing, including the date, time, requesting entity, purpose, and legal basis. Personal data is not stored in the log.

item.title: Kazakhstan Prosecutors Uncover Data Breaches in Schools, Violating Children's Privacy
item.description: Prosecutors in Kazakhstan's Uzunkol district have identified violations of personal data protection and information security in two schools. Officials shared student personal data with service providers without legal guardians' consent, and documents containing minors' data were publicly accessible on a school website. The school principal was fined, and measures were taken to rectify the breaches.

item.title: Former Kyrgyz Foreign Minister Criticizes Parliament's Work and Election System
item.description: Former Kyrgyz Foreign Minister Chingiz Aidarbekov has criticized the parliament's performance, the current election system, and the influence of money in elections. He stated that parliamentarians do not fully utilize their oversight powers over the executive branch. Aidarbekov also believes that a parliament elected solely through single-mandate districts is flawed.

item.title: Kyrgyz President Offers Condolences to Turkey Following Izmir Factory Explosion
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov of Kyrgyzstan has expressed deep sorrow to Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan following a fatal explosion at a metallurgical plant in Turkey's Izmir province. The Kyrgyz leader conveyed condolences to the families of the deceased and wished a speedy recovery to the injured on behalf of the people of Kyrgyzstan and himself.

item.title: Central Asian Nations and Azerbaijan Plan Unified QR Payment System
item.description: Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, and Azerbaijan are developing a unified QR payment system. This initiative aims to simplify cross-border payments for tourists, allowing them to use familiar banking apps. A joint working group will establish technical standards and security protocols for the integration.

item.title: Ukraine, Russia, and US Resume Peace Talks in Abu Dhabi After Nine-Month Hiatus
item.description: Ukraine, Russia, and the US have resumed three-way peace negotiations in Abu Dhabi following a nine-month pause. Discussions, which lasted over four hours on the first day, are set to continue. Delegations include high-level representatives from each country, with European nations participating in separate consultations.

item.title: Afghanistan Humanitarian Aid Appeal Only 33% Funded, UN Agency Reports
item.description: Afghanistan's 2026 humanitarian response plan has received only 32.7% of its required funding, leaving a shortfall of over $1.15 billion. Nearly 22 million people need assistance, making Afghanistan's funding requirement the largest among seven regional response plans. Aid organizations aim to reach 17.5 million people.

item.title: Turkmenistan's Halk Maslahaty Chairman Meets Turkish President and Business Leaders
item.description: Gurbanguly Berdimuhamedov, Chairman of Turkmenistan's Halk Maslahaty, visited Turkey for the COP31 climate conference. He met with Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan to discuss political, economic, and cultural cooperation. Berdimuhamedov also held meetings with executives from Rönesans Holding and Çalık Holding.

item.title: Tashkent Airport Temporarily Halts Customs Clearance for New Smartphones
item.description: Tashkent International Airport has temporarily suspended customs clearance for new, unregistered mobile phones. Devices are being seized for technical inspection due to increased attempts at illegal import using fake IMEI codes. The Customs Committee reported 185 cases of illegal mobile phone imports this year.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to Launch Proactive Death Registration Service in November
item.description: Kyrgyzstan plans to launch a proactive death registration service in November, eliminating the need for citizens to file a statement. Once a medical death certificate is issued, information will automatically transfer to the civil registry system, where a record will be created without citizen input. Relatives will only need to collect the physical certificate.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Constitutional Court Rules on Conditions for Judicial Bankruptcy of Citizens
item.description: Kazakhstan's Constitutional Court has addressed conditions for the judicial bankruptcy of citizens, specifically concerning Article 2 of the law on solvency restoration. The court noted that legislative criteria, including creditor categories, determine the application of bankruptcy procedures. A single case ruling does not indicate established legal practice.

item.title: Atyrau Deputy Akim Meirzhan Mukashev Resigns Amid Pre-trial Investigation
item.description: Meirzhan Mukashev has resigned as Deputy Akim of Atyrau of his own volition. This follows confirmation from the National Security Committee that a pre-trial investigation is underway against him. Unofficial reports suggest the investigation involves approximately 40 million tenge.

item.title: Uzbekistan Conducts Raids Against Drug Traffickers in Several Regions
item.description: Uzbekistan's State Security Service, along with other law enforcement agencies, has conducted operations against drug trafficking in multiple regions. Arrests were made in Gulistan, Navoi, Samarkand, and Karakalpakstan, with significant quantities of hashish, spice, and opium seized. Around ten individuals were detained, and criminal cases have been initiated.

item.title: Worker Dies During Construction at Almaty International Airport; Criminal Case Opened
item.description: A worker from a contracting company died during construction activities on the apron of Almaty International Airport. The Department of Transport Police has initiated a criminal case for violating labor safety regulations. The airport's press service confirmed the incident occurred in the construction area and is cooperating with the investigation.

item.title: Kyrgyz Parliament Forms Commission to Investigate Emergency Services Following Teen's Death
item.description: The Kyrgyz Parliament has established a deputy commission to investigate public services, prompted by the death of 14-year-old Amir Kunakov in the Ala-Archa gorge. The commission will examine emergency medical services and public service centers. Nine deputies have been appointed to the commission, which will also look into other cases beyond Kunakov's death.

item.title: Kazakhstan Seeks $40 Million Investor for New Potato Starch Plant
item.description: A new potato starch production facility is planned for the Aksu region in Kazakhstan's Pavlodar Oblast. The regional administration is actively seeking a potential investor for the project, estimated to cost $40 million. Investment teasers have been prepared to attract interested companies.

item.title: Kazakhstan Ministry Explains University Silence on Student's Death
item.description: Kazakhstan's Minister of Science and Higher Education, Sayasat Nurbek, stated that Al-Farabi Kazakh National University is refraining from commenting on a student's death due to ongoing investigations. Police have advised caution with statements during the procedural actions. The university has contacted the student's guardians and covered all expenses.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Gas Imports Surge, Exceeding Exports in Jan-Sep 2026
item.description: Uzbekistan's natural gas imports significantly surpassed exports in January-September 2026, reaching $1.605 billion, a nearly 50% increase year-on-year. September saw the highest monthly import volume. Gas exports decreased by 34.5% over the same period.

item.title: Uzbek President Meets New Secretary General of Turkic States Organization
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev of Uzbekistan met with the new Secretary General of the Organization of Turkic States (OTS), Mirvohid Azimov, during a working visit to Turkey. They discussed priorities for the organization and cooperation prospects. Preparations for the 2027 OTS summit in Uzbekistan were also a key topic.
